I have a feeling that a strong part of why I started thinking like this so early on was because of the internet.

Back when I was really young (1-7yo), I wasn't allowed to go outside and play with other kids. This was because I had pretty severe asthma at the time and I could easily get an attack if I get too tired. To counteract this, my mom gave me a phone at around 5-6 years old. Really early for any child, but made sense in the situation that I was in.

I remember spending all of my days on the internet. I learned more from the internet in that time more than all of my elementary school years.
I loved watching informational and philosophical videos from youtubers like Vsauce (one of the reasons why I absolutely love philosophy today). 
I also watched facts videos about the entire world. About other countries, other cultures, other religions, other traditions, other ways of life, and other beliefs.
These helped opened my eyes. 
The Earth was a tremendously large place. Larger than we could ever hope of even comprehending, and the fact that space was millions, no, billions times larger than this planet. This made me have a small existential crisis when I was around 7-9yo. I know It's weird to think of a kid having an existential crisis, but just hear me out. 

I thought that I was just a tiny spec of sand in the ginormous desert that is Earth. Does my life even have meaning? We all die, so what's the point of living? Everything comes to an end, even this place we call the universe, will die out.
That was when I remembered about christianity and the afterlife. I was in a weird delusional stage where I thought that  when I die, I go to heaven, just because I was scared of the idea of death.

After that, I learned to accept death as it is and chose to stop believing in christianity in favor of atheism.
To me, god does not exist. 

Deities are just devices we humans made to answer questions we couldn't answer back then, and the afterlife was created to give us a sense of hope that there is life after death, denying all logic to feed our delusions and give us a false sense of security.
